name: Celani Lemongrass-Coconut Fizz
description: A crisp, aromatic soda made with real lemongrass steam-extract and coconut water concentrate, lightly sweetened and carbonated at low pressure for a soft, almost still effervescence. Positioned as a 'wellness soda' in Tier 3 health markets.
flavor_profile: Clean, citrus-grassy lemongrass top note, smooth coconut body, very lightly sweet, almost medicinal clarity with a long, refreshing finish
cultural_context: Celani is the drink of Tier 3 professionals who want to signal health-consciousness without spending Tier 4 money. It's stocked in the lobbies of mid-grade corporate towers and at BCI-wellness clinics. There is a persistent, unverified rumor that Celani contains trace compounds that improve BCI latency — Celani's marketing team has never denied this explicitly.
story_hooks: The BCI latency rumor is true — not by design, but because a lemongrass cultivar mutation produces a compound with mild neural effects, and the company's internal researchers are desperately trying to quantify it before a regulatory body does.

A Celani distribution exec has been skimming product and reselling it at a markup to a Tier 1 underground wellness collective — the theft is small, but the collective has come to depend on it, and the exec is about to be caught.

A Tier 5 Spire resident has become obsessed with Celani despite having access to far more expensive beverages, visiting a Tier 3 market in disguise weekly — the question is whether this is eccentricity or something they're hiding from their household.
